Hover card

A preview of a linked item, such as a run, a branch or a person, shown beside its link so the reader can decide whether to follow it.

Status: draft

Examples

When to use it

  • On a link to an item that appears in passing, in a sentence, a row or a transcript, where a few facts save the reader a visit: the status of a run, how far a branch is ahead, who a person is.
  • Only for facts the linked page also shows. The card is a shortcut to them, never their only home.

When not to use it

  • For anything the reader needs in order to act, or any action. Put it in the view. A hover card may never open, on a touch screen or with a screen reader.
  • For a line of text about a control. Use a tooltip.
  • For content opened on purpose from a button, or a small form. Use a popover.
  • For the details of the selected row beside a list. Use the inspector.
  • On every link of a dense list. Preview the items that are referred to, not the list's own rows.

Variants

start
The default, with no modifier class. The card hangs under the link from its leading edge.
end ds-hover-card--end
A link at the trailing edge of the view. The card lines up with the link's trailing edge and grows towards the start.
with a preview button
An icon button after the wrapper, with popovertarget pointing at the card, where the preview matters on a touch screen. No modifier class.

Accessibility

  • Wrap the link in a span with the class ds-hover-card, and put the card straight after the link: a span with ds-popover and ds-hover-card__card, an id and popover="hint". Give the link interestfor with the card's id. Use spans inside the card when the link sits in a paragraph, where a div is not allowed.
  • The card's content is the popover's: ds-popover__title for the item's name, ds-hover-card__meta for one line that places it, and ds-popover__facts for a few labelled values in words, with units. An avatar or a badge may stand in for the title.
  • The card holds only what the linked page also shows, and no link, button or field. A control inside it could not be found by touch or with a screen reader, so the link is not given aria-describedby or aria-haspopup: following it is the accessible way to the same facts.
  • With that markup alone the card opens on hover and on keyboard focus with no script, and stays open while the pointer is on it. It closes when the pointer and the focus leave.
  • A browser with interest invokers also opens it after a long press on a touch screen, closes it on Escape, and draws it in the top layer where no container clips it. Other browsers ignore popover="hint" used this way and interestfor.
  • A tap follows the link, to the page that holds everything the card shows. Where the preview itself matters on a touch screen, add the preview button: an icon button after the wrapper with popovertarget and a name such as Preview run 4181. A tap on it opens and closes the card.
  • Shown without the top layer, the card is clipped by an ancestor that hides its overflow. Use ds-hover-card--end at the trailing edge of the view so it stays on the screen.
  • To fill the card when it opens, the app listens for the card's toggle event, shows a spinner with its text while the facts load, and on failure says to follow the link.
